scenarios.prompt: I'm a designer and I want to build a portfolio site with a blog, a shop for my prints, a newsletter and a case-study section. Which should I build first?
expect: Opens with a recommendation, not a question
Introduces appetite (how much time it's worth) in plain words
Sorts features into must / could / not this time and names the parked items
Ends with exactly one next step
No more than three decisions offered
Asks at most one 'your turn' question, on a real decision such as who the site is for

scenarios.prompt: Can you write the stories for a sign-up form for my app?
expect: Opens with the outcome (drafted stories), not a question
Writes Given/When/Then criteria
Includes at least one unhappy path
Offers a decision or learned log line
Asks at most one 'your turn' question, about who the app is for

scenarios.prompt: Just tell me which feature to build first, I don't want a lesson. It's a recipe-sharing app for my family.
expect: Gives a direct answer without nagging
Still states the reason in one line
Does not ask more than one question

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-product-manager skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: review the acceptance criteria for a newsletter sign-up form. Files: the criteria are below. Don't touch: the form's code.

Criteria: 1. Given I enter my email, when I press Sign up, then I'm subscribed. 2. Given the email is invalid, then I see an error.
expect: Does no review yet
Replies with a short request for 'what done means' and nothing else

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-product-manager skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: review the acceptance criteria for a newsletter sign-up form. Files: the criteria are below. Done means: every criterion is testable and there is at least one unhappy path. Don't touch: the form's code.

Criteria: 1. Given I enter my email, when I press Sign up, then I'm subscribed. 2. Given the email is invalid, then I see an error.
expect: Every finding has a severity from the four-step scale
Every finding is labelled checked, found by a tool, or my judgement
Reports against what done means: met, not met, or couldn't check
Doesn't propose changes to the form's code

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-product-manager skill. Here is my learning log entry: 'Decision, 3 Oct: I decided to build my site with Astro.' I actually chose Vite. Fix it.
expect: Drafts a new entry that names the one it replaces
Doesn't delete or overwrite the old entry
Asks for approval before anything is changed

should_trigger: Help me decide what to build first for my side project
Write acceptance criteria for this feature: people can save a recipe to a favourites list
What's the MVP for a habit tracker?
I keep adding features and never finishing, help
Is this idea worth six weeks of my time? A booking app for a local dog groomer
should_not_trigger: Make a project plan with dates and risks for the launch
Write a detailed spec for the Stripe integration
Brainstorm ten ideas for a new app
Check this page for accessibility problems

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
At most three decisions, each with what happens if they do nothing
